idea.title: Tally: a form builder that works like a doc

source.text: Tally: a form builder that works like a doc, free with a paid Pro plan, launch country BE (Belgium, selling worldwide online). Score it as of 2020-06-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: two bootstrapped developers. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug tally-forms.

idea.problem: Building a good-looking online form takes a drag-and-drop builder, and the polished ones (Typeform) charge for basics like responses and logic.
idea.customer: Makers, indie founders, no-code builders and small teams who need forms (waitlists, surveys, applications) and already work in doc-style tools like Notion
idea.solution: A web form builder you type into like a document (no drag-and-drop), with a generous free plan and a paid Pro plan for advanced features
claims: a form builder that works like a doc
free with a paid Pro plan

context.edge: two developers who can build the product themselves

assumptions: Pro price assumed at $29/month (USD, worldwide), in the range of Typeform's ~$40 average price (2018)
Bootstrapped: budget near zero beyond hosting and tools; founders' own time unpaid at first
Goal assumed to be a bootstrapped startup replacing two salaries
Main channel assumed organic: Product Hunt, maker communities and a 'Made with Tally' badge on free forms
Scored as of 2020-06-01 with evidence published on or before that date

confidence.note: No dated 2020 pricing pages, no form-specific free-to-paid benchmark, and no TAM report; archived pricing pages would raise it

gross_margin.note: Software: Stripe ~3% plus hosting; free users are a fixed hosting cost. ~93% (estimate).

ltv_cac.note: Organic CAC ~$60 gives LTV:CAC ~7.5 (estimate), but paid search would sink it; only the organic loop works.

pricing_power.note: Google Forms free and a generous own free plan anchor low; Pro must undercut Typeform's ~$40 ASP.

build_effort.note: A doc-style block editor plus logic, embeds and payments: about 2 months to a usable beta for two devs.

skills_match.note: Two developers: the build is their core skill; marketing and support are learnable.

capital_needed.note: Hosting from $7-25 per dyno per month; near-zero capital, fits a bootstrapped budget.

time_to_mvp.note: 8-10 weeks to a launchable editor (estimate); slower than a no-code test.

sales_cycle.note: Self-serve card checkout: a maker upgrades the day they hit a Pro feature.

channel_readiness.note: Channel exists: Typeform's 'powered by' badge was its top traffic source; no Tally audience yet.

search_demand.note: Mass need: Jotform 5M users (2019-07), SurveyMonkey 720,921 paying users (FY2019).

trend.note: Rising: SurveyMonkey revenue +21% (FY2019), Typeform revenue ~2x mid-2017 to mid-2018.

willingness_to_pay.note: Typeform ~40k paying customers at ~$40/month while users complain of rising prices.

free_alternatives.note: Google Forms is free with unlimited responses for basic forms (R5: free_alternative hit).

competitor_density.note: 10+ competitors incl. Typeform, Jotform, SurveyMonkey/Wufoo; strong leaders (R5 cap 3).

differentiation.note: Doc-style editing is a real but copyable UX difference; unlimited free is a pricing choice, not a moat.

legal_regulatory.note: GDPR processor duties (Art. 28 DPA) and EU VAT MOSS: compliance work, not a licence.

platform_dependency.note: Owns its product and badge channel; depends only on swappable Stripe and hosting.

market_risk.note: Forms are a durable, recurring business need, not a fad.

skills.note: Strong build skills; no stated track record selling SaaS.

assets.note: No audience, list or network stated.

interest.note: Motivation not stated; assumed curious builders.

tam.reasoning: Visible leaders' revenue: SurveyMonkey $307M (FY2019) + Jotform ~$54M ARR (2019) + Typeform ~$19M run rate (2018) = ~$380M, a lower bound

sam.reasoning: Self-serve form builders for makers and SMBs (Typeform + Jotform ~$73M plus Paperform, Wufoo, Formstack etc.), excluding enterprise survey spend: ~$100M

som.reasoning: 0.1% of SAM $100M in year 1 for two founders = $100k ARR

competitor_price_range.reasoning: Google Forms free; Typeform average price ~$40/month (2018 founder interview); no dated pricing pages for others

price.reasoning: Assumed Pro price below Typeform's ~$40 average price

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: Stripe ~3.1% blended (1.4%+€0.25 EU, 2.9%+€0.25 non-EU) = $0.9 + ~$1 infra and support per paying user

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Between Baremetrics' 7.7% SMB user churn (2017) and ProfitWell's 3-4% for larger plans (2019); low-priced self-serve plan

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Visitor to sign-up 10% x free to paid 2% (Jotform implied <3%: $54M ARR / $360 per year / 5M users)

cac.reasoning: Organic: ~200 founder hours x $30/h per 100 paying customers (Product Hunt, communities, badge loop). Paid search would be ~$9.88 CPC / 0.2% = ~$4,900

ltv_cac.reasoning: 452 / 60 on the organic channel only; below 0.1 on paid search

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Hosting 2 x $25 standard dynos + ~$50 database (Heroku pricing) + ~$50 tools; founders unpaid

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 150 / 27 = 6 paying customers for costs; ~220 to pay two modest salaries (€6k/month)

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 8-10 weeks build + launch + first upgrades within ~4 weeks

verdict.launch_reason: The founders are in Belgium, but the product sells online worldwide in English from day one; Belgium only sets the legal and VAT base.

rules_applied.effect: free_alternative hit: free_alternatives held at 2; strong_competitor hit: competitor_density held at 2 (cap 3); no score change

type_checks.note: SMB self-serve SaaS churns 5-8% a month (Baremetrics 7.7%, 2017); at $29/month, lifetime is ~17 months, so retention must be built in
A new form takes minutes to rebuild, so incumbents hold users mainly through existing embeds and integrations, not lock-in (estimate, no dated source)

verdict.cheapest_test: Landing page with a 60-second doc-style demo video, posted to Indie Hackers, r/nocode and Makerpad: 300 waitlist sign-ups and 10 annual Pro pre-orders in 7 days
kill_criteria: fewer than 150 waitlist sign-ups by day 7 -> rework the pitch before building
fewer than 5 Pro pre-orders at $29/month by day 14 -> rethink the paid plan
free-to-paid conversion below 1% after 90 days of launch -> change the Pro gate

rescue.change: Put a 'Made with Tally' badge on every free form and launch on Product Hunt, Indie Hackers and Notion/no-code communities
rescue.why: Turns the free plan into the channel (channel_readiness, ltv_cac), as Typeform's badge did
rescue.requires: A shipped free plan and a launch post

rescue.change: Gate a few high-value features (remove branding, custom domain, file uploads, team) in Pro and keep the rest free
rescue.why: Lifts free-to-paid conversion and pricing_power without killing the free hook
rescue.requires: Usage data on which features free users hit

narrative.answer: **GO**, barely. Demand is mass and rising, margins are software-grade and two developers can build it cheaply; the risk is a **crowded field** led by Typeform and free Google Forms, so the free plan must become the channel.
tldr: Forms are a mass, growing market: SurveyMonkey $307M (+21%), Jotform 5M users, Typeform ~$19M run rate.
Google Forms is free and Typeform is funded ($52M+): the doc-style editor is the only wedge.
Economics work only on organic growth: LTV:CAC ~7.5 organic, below 0.1 on paid search (estimates).

key_findings.title: Mass, rising demand for forms
key_findings.detail: SurveyMonkey grew revenue **21%** to $307M in FY2019 and Jotform hit **5M users** (2019-07).

key_findings.title: Leaders are strong, one is free
key_findings.detail: Typeform made **~$1.6M a month** (2018) on $52M+ raised; Google Forms does basic forms for **free**.

key_findings.title: The badge loop is the channel
key_findings.detail: Typeform's **'powered by' button** was its top traffic source, a free channel a generous free plan can copy.

narrative.recommendation: Build it, but ship the free plan with a 'Made with Tally' badge from day one and launch on Product Hunt; stop if free-to-paid stays under 1% after 90 days.
narrative.steelman: Typeform doubled revenue on a free-form badge loop while its users complain about rising prices; a doc-style builder with a generous free plan rides the same loop at near-zero CAC, in the year Notion made doc-style editing mainstream ($2B, 2020-04). The evidence supports this: no sub-score contradicts it.

premortem.cause: The generous free plan covers almost every need, so under 1% of users ever upgrade to Pro.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 5 Pro upgrades per 1,000 active free users in the first 30 days

premortem.cause: Launch noise fades among 10+ form tools; Typeform and Google Forms keep the makers.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 300 sign-ups from the Product Hunt launch week

premortem.cause: Pro users churn 7%+ a month after one-off projects, so revenue plateaus.
premortem.early_signal: More than 10% of month-1 Pro users cancel before month 2

changes.what: Notion reaches a $2B valuation: block-based, doc-style editing becomes a mainstream habit
Notion sees surging use as work moves home during COVID-19
Webflow raises $72M: the no-code movement draws money and makers
Typeform users complain of constant price increases and a shrinking free plan

why_now.note: A sourced shift in editing habits (Notion) and price frustration at the leader open the window.

icp.who: Makers, indie founders and no-code builders who build waitlists, surveys and applications and already work in Notion
where: Makerpad and the #nocode community on Twitter
icp.pays_for_today: Typeform at ~$40/month average (2018) or Google Forms for free
icp.trigger: Hitting Typeform's free-plan response limit or needing to remove branding on a launch form

customer.segment: Makers, indie founders and small teams who need good-looking forms
customer.pain: Polished forms cost ~$40/month; free ones look plain
customer.today: Typeform paid plans or Google Forms

free_alternative.evidence: Google Forms is free with unlimited responses in its own reporting (2017); TellForm is an open-source Typeform alternative (Product Hunt, 2018-12).

strong_competitor.evidence: Typeform: ~$1.6M a month revenue and ~40,000 customers (2018), $52M+ raised; SurveyMonkey $307M revenue (FY2019); Jotform 5M users (2019-07).

graveyard.evidence: Searched for form-builder shutdowns and post-mortems before 2020: none found; Wufoo sold to SurveyMonkey for a reported $35M (2011), an exit.

no_distribution.evidence: Clear: Typeform's 'powered by' button was its top traffic source (2017), and Wispform got 174 upvotes on Product Hunt (2019-08).

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Clear: Stripe 1.4% + €0.25 on EU cards (2016) and hosting from $25 per dyno per month (Heroku) leave ~93% gross margin (estimate).

weak_demand.evidence: Clear: SurveyMonkey revenue +21% in FY2019 and Jotform from 4M to 5M users in 10 months (2018-09 to 2019-07).

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Clear: GDPR Art. 28 processor duties (APD avis 98/2019) and EU VAT MOSS are compliance work; Schrems II pending, avoid by EU hosting.

saturated_wave.evidence: 4 look-alike form-builder launches found on Product Hunt in the window (Wispform, Tripetto for WordPress, Form-Builder, Webiny Form Builder): under 10.

competitors.name: Typeform
competitors.gap: Expensive; free plan limited; drag-and-drop style builder

competitors.name: SurveyMonkey / Wufoo
competitors.gap: Survey and enterprise focus, dated form UX

competitors.name: Wispform
competitors.gap: Cheaper Typeform clone, same builder style

customer_voice.quote: They keep removing features from their free and cheaper plan, making it impossible to use for free users
But expensive if you don't use it often

use_cases.name: Launch waitlists and sign-up forms for makers
Applications and lead forms for small businesses

scenarios.name: Pessimistic
scenarios.note: 0.5% of 8k free users upgrade after 12 months (estimate)

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: 3% of 20k free users, badge loop working (estimate)

risks.risk: Free plan too generous: conversion under 1%
risks.mitigation: Gate branding removal, custom domains and uploads in Pro

risks.risk: Typeform or Google copies doc-style editing
risks.mitigation: Ship faster and own the maker community

risks.risk: Phishing forms on the free plan hurt domain reputation
risks.mitigation: Abuse reporting and takedown from day one

risks.risk: US hosting transfer risk under the pending Schrems II ruling

test_plan.step: Record a 60-second demo of typing a form like a doc; build a landing page with a waitlist
Post on Indie Hackers, r/nocode, Makerpad and Twitter #nocode
Reply to every comment; offer an annual Pro pre-order at a launch discount
Interview 10 sign-ups on what they pay for forms today
test_plan.verify: 6 of 10 pay or have paid for a form tool

test_plan.step: Count sign-ups and pre-orders against the kill criteria
